study type: In vitro study using an animal model (mouse cortical neurons)
exposure: blocking neurotransmitter release with Tetanus toxin
cohort: The study participants were primary mouse cortical neurons of both sexes.
finding: Chronic network silencing triggers increased dense core vesicle (DCV) accumulation due to reduced exocytosis, and these accumulated DCVs can be released upon reactivation, leading to a massive potentiation of DCV exocytosis.
